newsitem.title: GERMANY: No date yet for military meeting on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: No date yet for military meeting on Zaire.

text.p: No firm date has yet been set for a meeting of military leaders from nations expected to send troops on an international peacekeeping mission to central Africa, a U.S. military spokesman in Germany said on Wednesday.
"We are expecting the meeting to be held on either Thursday or Friday but no firm date has been set," the spokesman at the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart told Reuters.
The meeting had initially been planned for Wednesday.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday several countries which wanted to take part in a military mission to eastern Zaire were now having second thoughts.
Kinkel said the Wednesday meeting had been postponed until Friday but the German foreign ministry said later it was up to U.S. military authorities in Stuttgart to make an official announcement.
Canadian Forces, in a statement issued by the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart, did not mention a date for the meeting but said that preliminary planning for the mission was underway.

Military officials in Stuttgart said the meeting time was likely to be set after talks between politicians on Thursday in New York to decide what help Rwandan refugees now need since thousands of people had begun returning to Rwanda from Zaire.

"The United Nations continues to re-evaluate the fluid situation in Central Africa. It would be premature to discuss options with contributing nations before a new mandate is issued," according to the statement from the Canadian Forces.

The statement said that the Canadian general marked to lead the mission, Lieutenant General Maurice Baril, "will reassess any changes of the mission being discussed by the United Nations and conduct further preliminary planning".

Military leaders from 14 nations, including France, Britain the United States and Canada, were expected to attend the meeting at the European Command headquarters in Stuttgart, which oversees U.S. military operations in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday that the United States has made no final decision on involvement of U.S. forces in relief efforts. U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said the United States was instead preparing for a military air relief operation.

Britain said on Wednesday that the multinational force was still probably needed since international agencies have said the situation in the region was still critical despite the return of refugees to Rwanda from eastern Zaire.
Kinkel said the subject of military involvement had also been discussed on Tuesday at a meeting of Western European Union in the Belgian port of Ostend.

"At that time the impression was that an international aid force would be necessary. Obviously some of the countries who wanted to take part have had somewhat different thoughts in the meantime," he said.
Kinkel did not say to which countries he was referring. Germany is not expected to send any troops.

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien had already said the Stuttgart meeting would probably be delayed until Friday. His foreign minister Lloyd Axworthy said the political meeting would be held on Wednesday.
